questions.question_text:
In a certain code language: Atoms cataract very small — 7#1 4%1 4*1 3!5; Smaller artifacts can vested — 8%1 6*1 5!5 2#1; Simple article clip verified — 6%1 5*9 7!5 3#9; Vents stay evoke crate — 3*1 4!5 4#1 4@5. The source working maps initial letters S→*, C→#, A→%, V→!, E→@.
Q. What is the code for ‘small’?
questions.explanation: The examples and the source’s initial-letter mapping identify S with *. The code shown for the five-letter word ‘small’ is 4*1.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8

In a certain code language: Atoms cataract very small — 7#1 4%1 4*1 3!5; Smaller artifacts can vested — 8%1 6*1 5!5 2#1; Simple article clip verified — 6%1 5*9 7!5 3#9; Vents stay evoke crate — 3*1 4!5 4#1 4@5. The source working maps initial letters S→*, C→#, A→%, V→!, E→@.
Q. Which of the following code can be coded for ‘vents smaller vested’?
questions.explanation: The initial-letter symbols required are ! for ‘vents’, * for ‘smaller’, and ! for ‘vested’. None of A–D has that ordered symbol pattern, so E is correct.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 9

Q. Which of the following can be the code for ‘verified small evoke cataract’?
questions.explanation: The source examples directly establish verified→7!5, small→4*1, evoke→4@5, and cataract→7#1. Their ordered sequence is option D.
